questions.q: What is the biological definition of 'movement' as a characteristic of living organisms?
a: An action by an organism or part of an organism causing a change of position or place
Only the locomotion of an entire animal from one habitat to another
The internal flow of blood through blood vessels
The growth of plant shoots toward sunlight

questions.q: Which term describes the chemical reactions in cells that break down nutrient molecules to release energy for metabolism?
What is 'sensitivity' defined as in living organisms?
a: The ability to increase in dry mass and cell number
The removal of toxic waste products of metabolism
The ability to detect or sense stimuli in the internal or external environment and to make appropriate responses
The process of absorbing minerals through roots

questions.q: How is 'growth' defined in biological terms for living organisms?
a: A temporary change in body posture due to muscular contraction
The production of offspring to pass on genetic information
The breakdown of complex food substances into simpler units
A permanent increase in size and dry mass by an increase in cell number or cell size or both

questions.q: What is the process that makes more of the same kind of organism called?
What is the biological definition of 'excretion'?
a: The passing of unabsorbed food out of the body as feces
The removal from organisms of toxic materials, the waste products of metabolism, and substances in excess of requirements
The intake of essential mineral ions from the soil
The active transport of water across a partially permeable membrane

questions.q: Which characteristic of living organisms is described as taking in materials for energy, growth, and development?
Which of the following correctly lists all seven characteristics of living organisms as defined by Cambridge IGCSE?
a: Movement, Respiration, Sensitivity, Growth, Reproduction, Excretion, Nutrition
Metabolism, Respiration, Secretion, Growth, Replication, Excretion, Nitrogen-fixation
Movement, Reaction, Sensation, Growth, Regeneration, Elimination, Digestion
Digestion, Respiration, Sensation, Generation, Reproduction, Evaporation, Nutrition

questions.q: Why is egestion (the removal of feces) not classified as excretion?
a: Because feces are not metabolic waste products produced by cells, but unabsorbed food passing through the gut
Because feces contain high amounts of active cellular energy
Because egestion only occurs in plants and not animals
Because feces are completely sterile and harmless

questions.q: Which process provides the chemical energy required for all other life processes to take place inside living cells?
A plant shoot bends toward a window as it grows. Which characteristic of living organisms is primarily demonstrated by this response?
Which of the following life processes involves the conversion of light energy into chemical energy in green plants?
Carbon dioxide is produced by human cells during respiration and is eliminated from the body through the lungs. What life process does this represent?
If an organism increases significantly in dry mass over time through cellular division, which life process has occurred?
A single-celled amoeba swims away from a highly concentrated salt solution. Which two characteristics are best demonstrated here?
Why are viruses generally considered by biologists to be on the border of living and non-living things?
a: They can perform all seven life processes independently without a host
They contain chloroplasts for independent photosynthesis
They can reproduce sexually through gametes
They display some characteristics of living organisms (like reproduction) only inside a living host cell, but lack others like independent respiration

questions.q: Which term describes all the chemical reactions that take place inside living organisms?
When a human touches a hot surface and immediately pulls their hand away, which characteristic allows them to detect the heat and respond?
Which of the following metabolic waste products must be excreted by mammals via the kidneys?
Which of the following best distinguishes living organisms from non-living machines?
a: Living things never change their internal chemical composition
Living things are made of metal components
Living things independently coordinate complex metabolic reactions, maintain homeostasis, and reproduce

questions.q: Why do green plants require nutrition even though they make their own food via photosynthesis?
a: To obtain inorganic ions (like nitrates and magnesium) and water needed for vital cellular molecules
To break down organic glucose into animal proteins
To eliminate the need for respiration

questions.q: Which characteristic ensures the survival of a species across generations rather than just an individual organism?
Sweating in humans helps remove excess heat and metabolic salts. While water and salts are excreted, sweating is primarily a mechanism for what?
How does growth in multicellular animals differ fundamentally from growth in most plants?
a: Animals grow only through root expansion
Plants do not undergo cellular division
Animals do not increase in dry mass
Animals generally grow throughout their whole body until adulthood, whereas plants often grow continuously at meristems (tips of roots and shoots)

questions.q: What is the primary reason living cells must continuously respire?
a: To supply ATP energy required to drive essential life processes and chemical reactions
To generate excess heat to burn food
To produce toxic wastes for excretion
To build up large starch granules

questions.q: Which life process involves breaking down large, insoluble food molecules into small, soluble molecules that can be absorbed?
An earthworm burrows deeper into damp soil when bright sunlight hits the surface. Which stimulus and response are occurring?
a: Stimulus: light, Response: movement away from light

questions.q: Which of the following substances is a primary waste product of cellular respiration that must be excreted by aerobic organisms?
Why is 'dry mass' used rather than 'fresh mass' when measuring true biological growth in plants?
a: Fresh mass fluctuates greatly depending on water content (hydration levels), whereas dry mass measures actual organic cellular material
Dry mass is easier to calculate mathematically
Fresh mass includes mineral ions from soil
Water has no mass in biological systems

questions.q: Which characteristic of living organisms involves detecting changes in external factors such as temperature, light intensity, or pressure?
Which of the following processes is a classic example of excretion in flowering plants?
a: Absorbing water through root hair cells
Dropping autumn leaves containing stored waste crystals, or releasing oxygen gas produced in photosynthesis

questions.q: Which of the following organisms exhibits all seven characteristics of life despite consisting of only a single cell?
What term describes the maintenance of a constant internal environment (such as internal body temperature and blood glucose) in living organisms?
Which characteristic is demonstrated when a yeast cell divides by budding to form a new individual?
What is the key difference between autotrophic nutrition (seen in plants) and heterotrophic nutrition (seen in animals)?
a: Animals produce their own glucose using sunlight
Plants feed on other dead organisms
Plants manufacture complex organic molecules from simple inorganic raw materials using light, whereas animals consume pre-formed organic molecules
Animals do not require any form of nutrition

questions.q: Which of the following processes represents an anabolic (building up) reaction that contributes directly to biological growth?
a: Assimilation converting absorbed amino acids into new cellular proteins

questions.q: Why is movement in plants generally slower and less obvious than movement in animals?
a: Plants move via growth responses (tropisms) or turgor changes rather than rapid muscular contractions
Plants do not possess cellular water
Plants lack any internal transport tissue
Plants do not undergo cellular respiration

questions.q: Which characteristic of life is directly linked to an organism's ability to avoid predators and locate food sources?
Which of the following correctly pairs a life process with its primary purpose?
a: Nutrition — providing chemical substances for energy and growth

questions.q: If a chemical substance is found inside a plant cell that is a poisonous byproduct of a metabolic pathway and is stored harmlessly in a vacuole, what process generated this fate?
